items.title: Rotation of the Earth
items.explanation: The Earth rotates on its own axis from West to East. This rotation takes approximately 24 hours to complete one full cycle. When viewed from above the North Pole, this movement appears as an anti-clockwise spin.

items.title: Why the Sun Appears to Move
items.explanation: The Sun does not actually move across the sky; it is the Earth that rotates beneath it. Because we observe the Sun from the rotating Earth, it creates the illusion that the Sun rises in the East and sets in the West.

items.title: Day and Night Cycle
items.explanation: As the Earth rotates from West to East, one side faces the Sun (daytime) while the opposite side faces away (nighttime). This rotation causes day and night to cycle across the globe.
